name: Vermont
summary: The state coat of arms on blue: a pine tree, a cow and sheaves of wheat in front of the Green Mountains, with a stag's head crest and the motto 'Freedom and Unity'.
origin: Vermont's earlier flags followed the US flag with stripes. The coat-of-arms flag was adopted on 1 June 1923. Before joining the US in 1791, Vermont was an independent republic (1777–1791).

symbols.name: Cow and wheat
symbols.description: A cow and three sheaves of wheat.

symbols.name: Pine branches
symbols.meaning: The Vermonters who wore pine sprigs at the Battle of Plattsburgh in 1814.

history.label: Stripes flag
history.note: US-style stripes with the arms in the canton.

facts: The Green Mountain Boys flag, green with a blue canton of 13 stars, is also widely flown.
Vermont was an independent republic from 1777 to 1791.
The motto 'Freedom and Unity' balances individual liberty and common good.
clues: A coat of arms with a pine, a cow and wheat in front of green mountains, on blue.
Its state was an independent republic before joining the Union in 1791.
